text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - Shares ended higher for a third day, as worries over next week's budget eased and nerves were calmed by a firm early showing on Wall Street. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,657.9, up 17.9 points, or 0.39 percent.

FRANKFURT - Shares notched up more records as the blue chip DAX reached an all-time high close, but profit-taking took the edge off the market's advance. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,805.29, up 6.78 points, or 0.18 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 3,820.16, up 0.64 points, or 0.02 percent.

PARIS - Stocks hit a record closing high, with Rhone-Poulenc shares leaping by nearly 20 percent after news that the chemicals and drugs firm planned to buy out its U.S. subsidiary Rhone-Poulenc Rorer. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,893.64, up 26.20 points, or 0.91 percent.

ZURICH - Shares managed to post another record close even though they slipped back from early gains to end near the day's lows. The Swiss market index closed at 5,669.9, up 7.5 points, or 0.13 percent.

MILAN - Shares closed lower but above session troughs with the rally of recent days petering out for the moment on selective profit-taking which dealers said demonstrated signs of emerging nervousness. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 13,407, down 62 points, or 0.46 percent.

AMSTERDAM - Shares closed mixed to lower with early gains eroded by profit-taking, although a late spike higher on the back of a firmer Wall Street opening helped to bring prices above the session's low. The AEX index closed at 870.63, down 0.83 points, or 0.10 percent.
TOKYO - Stocks closed slightly lower as an upbeat mood carried over from the previous day finally fizzled out. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,624.76, down 54.51 points, or 0.26 percent.

HONG KONG - Stocks closed modestly higher after gains were trimmed by investors taking profits before the three-day market holiday next week marking Hong Kong's handover on July 1, brokers said. The Hang Seng index closed at 15,128.02, up 63.00 points, or 0.42 percent.

SYDNEY - Shares closed slightly weaker after the market almost fully recovered from early selling triggered by a weaker copper price and a lower finish from the Dow on Wednesday. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,699.9, down 5.2 points, or 0.19 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - The industrial and all-share indices finished at record closing highs in active trade, boosted by a host of positive news. The All-share index closed at 7,402.7, up 48.7 points, or 0.66 percent. The All Gold index closed at 1,008.8, up 1.4 points, or 0.84 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,742.3, up 72.4 points, or 0.14 percent.
